implementation_notes: Kotlin models a monoid as an extension or a companion object exposing operator fun plus(): combine and a Zero/identity value, so the built-in folds (fold, reduce, associate) work unchanged. Kotlin's collections are the practical home of monoids: List.plus is the concatenation monoid with an empty list identity, and Sequence has a running fold that never materialises the source. The trap is operator resolution - defining plus on a data class can silently change the meaning of every existing + on that type, including inside libraries that use it for a different purpose.
idiom_name: operator fun plus() as combine; companion object Zero/identity; Sequence.fold for streaming
pitfalls: operator plus on a domain type changes the meaning of every existing + on that type, including uses inside third-party libraries that expect numeric addition.
plusAssign on a MutableList mutates in place and is NOT the same operation as plus - mixing them breaks the associativity assumption in a fold.
fold with an initial value is required; fold { a, b -> } without one throws on an empty sequence rather than returning the identity.
Combining large lists with + copies the left operand each time; append into a MutableList and convert once if the result must be a List.
